result.response:
Scope of review
- Architecture correctness and security of: identity provider, credential lifecycle, session/token management, client flows, service-to-service auth, privilege model, auditing/observability, and operational resilience.

Artifacts needed
- High-level diagram: components, trust boundaries, data stores, external IdP/SMTP/SMS, gateways, mobile/web apps.
- Sequence diagrams for: sign-up, login, refresh, logout, password reset, email/phone verify, MFA enrollment/challenge, SSO, service-to-service calls.
- Configs/policies: token formats/claims, lifetimes, rotation, cookie settings, hashing params, CORS, CSRF, rate limits, lockouts.
- Code/infra pointers: auth middleware, token mint/verify, session store, secret management, key management, CI/CD.
- Threat model notes and compliance requirements (e.g., GDPR, SOC2, HIPAA).
- Metrics/logs samples and incident runbooks.

Evaluation checklist
1) Identity and accounts
- Account types: human vs service; single vs multi-tenant isolation.
- Unique identifiers, email/phone verification, username normalization.
- Recovery flows: secure email magic link or TOTP backup codes; takeover-resistant.

2) Credentials and MFA
- Password hashing: Argon2id (preferred) or scrypt; strong params; per-user salt; pepper (HSM/KMS-backed) optional.
- MFA: WebAuthn/passkeys preferred; TOTP as fallback; SMS only as last resort; step-up MFA for risky ops; recovery codes.

3) Sessions and tokens
- Web: server-side sessions via HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Lax/Strict cookies; rotate session ID post-auth; CSRF protection.
- APIs/mobile/SPAs: OAuth2.1/OIDC Authorization Code with PKCE; short-lived access token; refresh token rotation with reuse detection.
- Token type: opaque (introspect) or JWT; if JWT, short TTL (5–15 min), aud/iss/exp/nbf, kid, jti; sign with asymmetric keys; no PII in claims.
- Logout: server session invalidation; refresh token revocation list.

4) SSO and federation
- OIDC/SAML with external IdPs; map attributes to internal subjects; just-in-time provisioning rules; SCIM for lifecycle.

5) Service-to-service auth
- OAuth2 Client Credentials with audience scoping and least privilege, or mTLS with SPIFFE/SPIRE; rotate client secrets/keys.

6) Authorization
- RBAC at minimum; consider ABAC/claims-based and policy engine (OPA/Cedar) for complex domains; centralized policy evaluation; consistent permission caching with invalidation.

7) Secrets and keys
- Secrets in vault/KMS; no in-repo; environment scoping; rotation policies.
- Token signing keys: asymmetric, stored in HSM/KMS; JWKS endpoint with caching and key rollover; publish kid.

8) Transport and browser security
- Enforce TLS 1.2+ everywhere; HSTS, secure ciphers.
- Cookies: HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite; partitioned if needed; no tokens in localStorage.
- CORS: explicit allowlist, no wildcard with credentials.

9) Abuse prevention
- Per-username/IP rate limits and anomaly detection on auth endpoints.
- Bot protection, CAPTCHA only after risk signals.
- Lockout with backoff; notify user on sensitive changes.

10) Observability and audit
- Structured logs with trace IDs; log auth events (who, what, when, where, result, jti).
- Metrics: login success/fail, MFA enrollment/challenge, token mint/refresh/reject, latency, 4xx/5xx, RL triggers.
- Alerts for spikes, reuse-detected refresh, signature/clock skew errors.
- Privacy: minimize logs; redact PII and secrets.

11) Resilience and scale
- IdP horizontally scalable; stateless where possible; session store (Redis) HA and scoped TTLs.
- JWKS caching with refresh; clock skew handling.
- Backpressure and circuit breakers around external email/SMS/IdP.
- Disaster recovery: key backup/restore, tenant export, break-glass admin.

12) Compliance and data
- Data retention/erasure for auth logs and identifiers; consent and purpose limitation.
- Regional data residency if required.

Reference architectures
- Web app (first-party):
  - Server-side sessions with cookie; CSRF token + SameSite; store session in Redis; rotate on privilege change; optional WebAuthn for MFA.
- SPA/mobile + API:
  - OIDC provider (Auth0/Keycloak/Cognito/ForgeRock).
  - Authorization Code + PKCE; access token JWT (5–10 min); refresh token rotation; store refresh token in secure httpOnly cookie for web; Secure Enclave/Keychain for mobile.
  - Resource servers validate JWT via JWKS; enforce aud/scope; no introspection on hot path.
- Microservices:
  - Gateway validates external tokens and issues internal short-lived JWT or mTLS identities; per-service audiences; optionally service mesh with mTLS and SPIFFE IDs; centralized policy check.

Threat considerations
- Account takeover: phishing, SIM swap, OAuth token theft; mitigate with WebAuthn, device binding, refresh rotation with reuse detection, IP/device risk.
- CSRF/XSS: prefer cookies + CSRF or full token binding; strict CSP; output encoding.
- Replay: short TTL, jti with one-time use for sensitive operations; TLS.
- Key compromise: rotation drills, KMS, narrow blast radius via short TTL and audience scoping.
- Enumeration: uniform responses and timing, RL per identifier.

Performance tips
- JWT verification: cache JWKS keys and kid mapping; pre-warm; consider local JIT authz cache with bounded TTL.
- Password hashing: tune Argon2id params to ~100–250ms/server; adaptive.
- Keep token size small (<2KB) to fit headers.

Open questions
- Which clients (web SPA, SSR, mobile, IoT) and flows are in scope?
- Are you using an external IdP or building in-house? Which one?
- Token choice: JWT vs opaque; current TTLs; rotation strategy; revocation model?
- Where are tokens/cookies stored on each client? Any use of localStorage?
- Current password hashing algorithm and parameters?
- MFA methods enabled and enrollment UX?
- Session store technology and eviction/rotation policy?
- Authorization model (RBAC/ABAC); where are policies enforced?
- How do services authenticate to each other? Any mesh/gateway?
- Secret storage and key management solution?
- Current rate limiting, anomaly detection, and bot controls?
- Audit log schema and retention; access controls on logs?
- Compliance constraints (GDPR/CCPA/HIPAA) and data residency?
- Incident response: how to invalidate tokens at scale; key rotation runbook?

Next steps
- Share the requested artifacts and answers to open questions.
- I will produce a gap analysis mapped to the checklist, prioritized recommendations, and an implementation plan with risk and effort estimates.
